existing_roles.title: Senior Director, Quality Control
existing_roles.description:
Crescent Biopharma’s vision is to build a world leading oncology company bringing the next wave of therapies for cancer patients. The Company’s clinical-stage pipeline includes its lead program, a PD-1 x VEGF bispecific antibody, as well as novel antibody-drug conjugates. By leveraging multiple modalities and established targets, Crescent aims to rapidly advance potentially transformative therapies as single agents and as part of combination regimens to treat a range of solid tumors. For more information, visit www.crescentbiopharma.com and follow the Company on LinkedIn and X.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Director, Quality Control to join as a key leader within Crescent's Quality organization, responsible for providing strategic and hands-on Quality Control leadership across company’s biologics and ADC programs, and future pipeline growth. Partnering closely with Analytical Sciences, GMP Quality Assurance, CMC/Technical Operations, Supply Chain, and Regulatory Affairs, you will provide phase-appropriate QC oversight from early development through late-stage development and commercialization within a global outsourced testing and manufacturing network. You will ensure reliable release and stability testing while building the QC infrastructure, laboratory network, and operating controls needed to advance programs into Phase 3, PPQ, BLA/MAA submission, and commercial readiness.

Crescent's operating model requires clear, collaborative accountability between Analytical Sciences and QC. Analytical Sciences leads analytical development and performs the primary technical work through method development, characterization, qualification, validation strategy, and PPQ readiness. QC provides oversight and operational input during early development, assumes increasing responsibility for method transfer, validation execution oversight, laboratory readiness, and GMP testing as programs mature, and takes primary ownership of routine QC operations and analytical method lifecycle management following transition to late-stage and commercial operations.

Success in this role requires a collaborative, hands-on leader who understands both analytical development and commercial QC operations, can establish effective governance across internal and external partners, and thrives in a fast-paced biotechnology environment while balancing scientific rigor, compliance, speed, and pragmatism.

### **Responsibilities**

* Define and implement Crescent's phase-appropriate QC strategy and operating model across early development, Phase 3, PPQ, regulatory submission, and commercialization, with clear decision rights and handoffs among Analytical Sciences, QC, and GMP QA.
* Oversee QC activities for drug substance, drug product, intermediates, finished goods, in-process, release, characterization, and stability testing across the portfolio.
* Provide QC oversight and operational requirements during early development while Analytical Sciences leads method development, characterization, qualification, validation strategy, and method maturation through PPQ readiness.
* Partner with Analytical Sciences on integrated Phase 3 and PPQ readiness, including method validation and transfer, laboratory qualification, specifications, reference standards and critical reagents, stability, sample management, and testing timelines.
* Lead QC execution oversight for method transfer, validation, and laboratory readiness; following transition to GMP QC operations, own routine method lifecycle management, performance monitoring, changes, revalidation, transfers, and remediation.
* Lead outsourced GMP QC operations, including sample management and testing coordination, and ensure timely, compliant release and stability testing for clinical supply, PPQ, batch disposition, regulatory commitments, and future commercial supply.
* Partner with Analytical Sciences, CMC, Regulatory Affairs, and QA on specifications and stability strategy; lead operational implementation, stability execution, data review, trending, and escalation within the QC network.
* Establish and oversee reference standard and critical reagent programs, including qualification, bridging, inventory, monitoring, replacement, and lifecycle planning.
* Provide technical leadership for OOS, OOT, OOE, atypical results, invalid assays, laboratory deviations, CAPAs, and change controls, ensuring scientifically sound, timely investigations and risk-based escalation.
* Lead selection, onboarding, qualification, governance, and performance management of CDMO QC functions and contract laboratories, including agreements, capacity, metrics, issue management, data integrity, and inspection readiness.
* Provide QC input to CMC and regulatory strategies and support IND/IMPD, BLA/MAA, health authority, and inspection activities; ensure commitments are implemented within the laboratory network.
* Lead alliance management with business partners on QC matters, including governance, roles and responsibilities, shared testing and release requirements, issue escalation, decision-making, and alignment on development, regulatory, and future commercial priorities.
* Establish scalable QC procedures, systems, metrics, budgeting, forecasting, and resource plans; support compliant use of LIMS, stability, analytical data, and trending tools, and build internal QC capability as Crescent advances toward commercialization.
* Mentor staff and consultants and foster a culture of scientific rigor, collaboration, accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement while staying current with evolving GMP, ICH, compendial, and industry expectations.

### **Education & Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in life sciences, analytical sciences, biochemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* A minimum 10-12 years of progressive experience in biologics QC, analytical development, or related CMC functions, including leadership of GMP QC operations in an outsourced environment.
* Experience with biologics analytical methods, including cell-based bioassays/potency assays; ADC and other complex biologic modality experience is preferred.
* Experience supporting biologics from clinical development through Phase 3, PPQ, BLA/MAA, and commercial readiness; bispecific antibody, ADC, or other complex modality experience is a plus.
* Proven experience transitioning methods from development into routine GMP QC use, including qualification, validation, transfer, implementation, performance monitoring, and lifecycle management.
* Strong experience with release and stability testing, specifications, reference standards and critical reagents, OOS/OOT/OOE investigations, analytical trending, deviations, CAPAs, and change control.
* Demonstrated success overseeing CDMO QC functions and contract laboratories, including qualification, governance, investigations, capacity, performance, and issue resolution.
* Strong knowledge of global GMP regulations, FDA/EMA/ICH guidance, compendial expectations, data integrity, Part 11 / Annex 11, and phase-appropriate application across development and commercial operations.
* Experience supporting regulatory submissions, health authority questions, pre-approval inspections, and commercial inspection readiness.
* Ability to establish clear roles and effective collaboration among Analytical Sciences, QC, GMP QA, CMC/Technical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, and external partners.
* Strategic thinker with a hands-on approach, solutions-oriented leader who communicates clearly, applies pragmatic science- and risk-based judgment, works effectively in a fast-paced small-company environment, and can travel to external sites as needed.
* Commitment to living Crescent’s core values and operating norms.

### **What We Offer**

* Opportunity to join a mission-driven team where you'll contribute to impactful work, take on varied responsibilities, and grow quickly in a dynamic environment
* Competitive compensation, including base salary, performance bonus, and equity
* 100% employer-paid benefits package
* Flexible PTO
* Two, one-week company-wide shutdowns each year
* A commitment to your professional development, with access to resources, mentorship, and growth opportunities

### **Salary Range**

The salary range for this position is $260,000 to $285,000. The final salary offered will depend on several factors, which may include, but is not limited to relevant years of experience, educational background, and geography.

**Additional Description for Pay Transparency:**

The final salary offered will depend on several factors, which may include, but is not limited to relevant years of experience, educational background, and geography. Subject to the terms of their respective plans, employees and/or eligible dependents are eligible to participate in the following Company sponsored employee benefit programs: medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short- and long-term disability. Subject to the terms of their respective plans, employees are eligible to participate in the Company’s savings plan (401(k)). This position is eligible to participate in the Company’s long-term incentive program. Subject to the terms of their respective policies and date of hire, Employees are eligible for the following time off benefits: Vacation – Unlimited PTO; Sick time – 10 days per calendar year; Holiday pay, including two Company shut downs; Parental Leave – 16 weeks within one year of the birth/adoption/foster care of a child; FMLA; Military Leave. Additional information can be found - https://www.crescentbiopharma.com/careers/#benefits

Please note:

Crescent Biopharma is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace where all individuals are valued and respected. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status.

**Please note, Crescent does not accept unsolicited resumes from external agencies or recruiters. Submission of a resume without a prior written agreement does not create any express or implied contract between Crescent and the agency. Crescent will not pay any fees related to unsolicited resumes.**

existing_roles.description:
**Since 1869, we've connected people through food they love. We’re proud to be stewards of amazing brands that people trust. Our portfolio includes the iconic Campbell’s brand, as well as Cape Cod, Chunky, Goldfish, Kettle Brand, Lance, Late July, Pacific Foods, Pepperidge Farm, Prego, Pace, Rao’s Homemade, Snack Factory, Snyder’s of Hanover. Swanson, and V8.**

**Here, you will make a difference every day. You will be supported to build a rewarding career with opportunities to grow, innovate and inspire. Make history with us.**

**Why Campbell’s…**

* Benefits begin on day one and include medical, dental, short and long-term disability, AD&D, and life insurance (for individual, families, and domestic partners).
* Employees are eligible for our matching 401(k) plan and can enroll on the first day of employment with immediate vesting.
* Campbell’s offers unlimited sick time along with paid time off and holiday pay.
* If in WHQ – free access to the fitness center. Access to on-site day care (operated by Bright Horizons) and company store.
* Giving back to the communities where our employees work and live is very important to Campbell’s. Our “Campbell’s Cares” program matches employee donations and/or volunteer activity up to $1,500 annually.
* Campbell’s has a variety of Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) to support employees.

**Sr. Director, Supply Quality and Warehouse and Distribution Quality**

The Sr. Director, Supply Quality and Warehouse and Distribution Quality is responsible for leading a comprehensive supply quality, warehouse quality, and distribution quality program across ingredients, packaging, suppliers, warehouses, distributors, and external partners. This role partners closely with Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain, R&D, Regulatory, Legal, plant operations, warehouse and distribution teams, suppliers, brokers, distributors, customers, and third parties to drive quality, compliance, supply continuity, and execution excellence. The director establishes and executes strategy, strengthens governance and systems, leverages data and digital tools to proactively manage risk, serves as a key customer interface, and owns critical customer quality relationships to build trust, resolve issues, and deliver on customer, consumer, brand, and business expectations.

 

**What you will do…**

* Strategic Leadership: Define, communicate, and execute the supply quality and warehouse and distribution quality strategy, roadmap, objectives, and programs across the supply network. Lead with a systems-thinking approach to prioritize risk, align resources, and drive measurable results.
* Category and Network Oversight: Provide leadership across ingredient, packaging, supplier, warehouse, and distributor categories, applying deep quality expertise to materials, storage, handling, processes, and network performance.
* Standards and Systems Management: Establish, interpret, communicate, and strengthen policies, standards, procedures, specifications, verification, and validation processes to ensure consistent execution of warehouse, distribution, regulatory, and quality expectations.
* Risk and Compliance Leadership: Identify, assess, and mitigate quality, regulatory, operational, and reputational risks across the supply base, warehouse network, and distribution network. Oversee risk assessments, ratings, audits, compliance, nonconformances, and business continuity actions.
* Audit and Verification Oversight: Lead audit strategy and governance, including planning, auditor capability development, execution oversight, corrective action follow-up, and continuous improvement of supplier, warehouse, and distributor verification programs.
* Performance Management and Analytics: Lead the use of metrics, data analytics, digital tools, and AI-enabled insights to monitor supplier, warehouse, and distributor performance, identify trends, accelerate decision-making, and improve accountability, transparency, and consistency.
* Supplier, Warehouse, and Distributor Performance: Oversee relationship management, improvement initiatives, contract and performance reviews, and resource deployment to improve quality, compliance, and service outcomes across the network.
* Regulatory and Industry Leadership: Apply deep knowledge of applicable regulations and industry expectations to guide program design, ensure compliance, and influence best-in-class execution across the supply, warehouse, and distribution network.
* Customer Interface and Relationship Ownership: Serve as a key customer interface for quality-related matters and own strategic customer relationships. Build credibility and trust, lead quality discussions, respond to customer concerns, align on expectations, and drive effective resolution of quality, compliance, and service issues.
* Cross-Functional and Enterprise Collaboration: Partner across supply chain, quality, regulatory, legal, R&D, operations, and external stakeholders to align priorities, influence change, and deliver integrated solutions that protect the business and strengthen performance.
* People and Resource Leadership: Lead, coach, and develop talent while overseeing internal, supplier, and third-party resources. Build a high-performing team environment focused on accountability, capability building, and continuous improvement.
Benchmarking and Continuous Improvement: Benchmark internal and external best practices, incorporate learnings into systems and processes, and drive future-ready capabilities across supply quality and warehouse and distribution quality. 

 

**Who you will work with…**

Collaborate closely with Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain, R&D, Legal, Regulatory, plant operations, warehouse and distribution teams, suppliers, distributors, brokers, customers, and third-party partners.

 

**What you bring to the table… (Must Have)**

* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in a relevant field preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive quality, supply quality, warehouse quality, or distribution quality management experience in food manufacturing, consumer products, logistics, or a related industry.
* Demonstrated leadership in supplier quality, warehouse and distribution quality systems, regulatory compliance, and cross-functional program management.
* Strong capability in risk assessment, strategic planning, stakeholder influence, data-driven decision-making, and leading through complexity.
* Experience leading teams, developing talent, and managing external partners and third-party resources.
Ability to travel up to 50% depending on business, audit, and project needs. 

 

**It would be great to have… (Nice to Have)**

* Experience in supplier quality, warehouse quality, distribution quality, manufacturing operations, or managing complex supply networks in a CPG, food, or logistics environment.
* Certifications such as ASQ, HACCP, PCQI, GFSI, auditing, Six Sigma, Lean, or project management.
* Strong knowledge of quality systems, supplier management, audit programs, warehouse and distribution practices, and applicable FDA, USDA, CFIA, and related regulatory requirements.
Experience leveraging systems, analytics, and digital tools to strengthen visibility, compliance, and performance management. 

 

**Compensation and Benefits:**

The target base salary range for this full-time, salaried position is between

$203,000-$279,200

Individual base pay depends on work location and additional factors such as experience, job-related skills, and relevant education or training. Total pay may include other forms of compensation. In addition, we offer competitive health, dental, 401k and wellness benefits beginning on the first day of employment. Please ask your Talent Acquisition Partner for more information about our total rewards package.

existing_roles.title: Plant Manager- tissue and paper manufacturing
existing_roles.description:
This is a high-impact leadership opportunity for a proven manufacturing executive with deep **paper manufacturing and paper machine operations experience**. Our client is seeking a hands-on, results-driven leader who can take full ownership of plant performance, strengthen operational discipline, and lead the facility to improved results across **safety, quality, production, reliability, cost and people development**.

The successful candidate will be responsible for all aspects of plant operations and will play a key role in driving performance improvements, stabilizing underperforming areas, and building a strong culture of accountability, teamwork and continuous improvement.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

This role is ideal for a seasoned Plant Manager or senior operations leader who understands the complexity of paper manufacturing and has a track record of improving plant performance through strong leadership, technical knowledge, disciplined execution and data-driven decision-making.

The Plant Manager will oversee the day-to-day and strategic leadership of the facility, ensuring the plant operates safely, efficiently and profitably while developing both leadership and frontline teams.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Lead all plant operations to achieve established **safety, quality, production, reliability and financial objectives**.
* Build and reinforce a strong **safety culture** through visible leadership, clear expectations, coaching and accountability at all levels of the organization.
* Oversee plant performance and ensure operations are aligned with productivity, quality and cost targets.
* Optimize **paper machine performance**, equipment uptime, production output and finished-product quality.
* Improve equipment reliability through strong maintenance systems, including preventive and predictive maintenance, planning and scheduling, and root cause analysis.
* Manage and improve plant financial performance, including cost-per-ton, labour, maintenance, fibre, chemical and energy costs.
* Lead continuous improvement efforts using structured, data-driven problem-solving methodologies to improve operational and financial results.
* Develop and execute recovery or turnaround plans for underperforming operations, establishing clear priorities, ownership, milestones and measurable outcomes.
* Build, coach and strengthen plant leadership, technical and hourly teams through employee development, performance management, succession planning and accountability.
* Partner with maintenance, production, quality and leadership teams to ensure cross-functional alignment and effective execution of plant priorities.
* Establish a culture focused on **performance, engagement, ownership and continuous improvement**.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for a strong plant leader with deep technical and operational knowledge of **paper manufacturing**, particularly **paper machine operations**, who can lead a large team and drive measurable business results.

**Qualifications & Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in **Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing** or a related field is preferred.

existing_roles.description:
Description:

**Plant Manager** 
**Location:** United Rolls Inc. In Canton, Ohio 
**Department:** Operations 
**Reports To:** President 
**FLSA Status:** Exempt

**Position Summary**

The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, performance, safety, quality, and profitability of United Rolls Inc.'s manufacturing operations, including an iron foundry and machine shop specializing in the production of centrifugal spun cast iron rolls for the steel, aluminum, paper, plastics, and other industrial processing industries. This position directs all aspects of production, maintenance, quality assurance, engineering, environmental compliance, and workforce development to ensure on-time delivery of world-class products while maintaining the highest standards of safety, quality, and operational excellence.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

**Safety and Environmental Leadership**

* Establish and maintain a strong safety culture throughout the foundry and machine shop operations.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, state environmental regulations, and company safety policies.
* Lead incident investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective actions.
* Conduct regular safety audits, risk assessments, and safety training programs.
* Drive continuous improvement in safety metrics, including reduction of recordable incidents and near misses.

**Operations Management**

* Direct daily operations of the iron foundry, centrifugal casting processes, heat treatment operations, roll finishing, and machine shop activities.
* Ensure production schedules meet customer delivery requirements while maintaining efficiency and quality standards.
* Monitor plant productivity, capacity utilization, scrap rates, and operational performance metrics.
* Coordinate production planning, workflow optimization, and resource allocation.
* Implement Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and continuous improvement initiatives.

**Foundry Management**

* Oversee all foundry operations including:
* Melting and pouring of iron alloys.
* Centrifugal casting of rolls.
* Mold preparation and handling.
* Heat treatment processes.
* Metallurgical testing and quality control.
* Ensure proper process controls are maintained to achieve customer specifications and metallurgical requirements.
* Drive improvements in yield, casting quality, and process consistency.

**Machine Shop Leadership**

* Manage machining operations involving large CNC and manual equipment used in roll finishing.
* Optimize machine utilization, tooling performance, setup reduction, and throughput.
* Ensure proper maintenance and calibration of machine tools and inspection equipment.
* Support implementation of advanced machining technologies and automation where appropriate.

**Quality Assurance**

* Partner with Quality and Metallurgical teams to ensure product integrity.
* Lead efforts to reduce defects, rework, customer complaints, and warranty claims.
* Ensure compliance with ISO and customer quality standards.
* Review and analyze quality metrics and implement corrective actions.

**Maintenance and Reliability**

* Direct preventive and predictive maintenance programs for foundry and machining equipment.
* Develop capital improvement and equipment replacement plans.
* Minimize downtime through effective maintenance planning and reliability strategies.
* Oversee utilities, plant infrastructure, and critical support systems.

**Financial Management**

* Develop and manage annual operating budgets.
* Monitor labor, material, energy, maintenance, and overhead costs.
* Identify and implement cost reduction initiatives.
* Analyze production and operational data to maximize profitability.
* Support capital investment planning and ROI analysis.

**Leadership and Workforce Development**

* Lead, coach, and develop supervisors, managers, and hourly employees.
* Foster employee engagement, accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
* Support workforce planning, succession planning, and talent development efforts.
* Collaborate with Human Resources on hiring, performance management, and employee relations.
* Maintain positive labor-management relationships where applicable.

**Customer and Business Support**

* Support sales and customer service teams by ensuring manufacturing capabilities align with customer requirements.
* Participate in customer visits, audits, and technical reviews.
* Work closely with engineering on new product development and process improvements.
* Maintain strong communication with suppliers and contractors.

**Position Impact**

The Plant Manager plays a critical leadership role in ensuring United Rolls Inc. delivers high-quality spun cast iron rolls safely, efficiently, and profitably while driving continuous improvement and supporting the company's long-term growth objectives.

Requirements:

**Qualifications**

**Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Metallurgy, Industrial Management, or related field preferred.
* Equivalent combination of education and industry experience may be considered.

**Experience**

* Minimum 10 years of manufacturing leadership experience.
* Minimum 5 years in a plant management, operations management, or senior production leadership role.
* Strong experience in foundry operations, metal casting, steel or iron manufacturing, heavy industrial manufacturing, or related industries.
* Experience managing machining operations and large CNC equipment preferred.
* Proven success leading safety, quality, productivity, and continuous improvement initiatives.

**Technical Knowledge**

* Iron metallurgy and centrifugal casting processes.
* Foundry operations and heat treatment processes.
* CNC machining and machining best practices.
* Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Quality management systems and root cause analysis.
* Maintenance and reliability management.
* ERP/MRP manufacturing systems.
* OSHA and environmental compliance standards.

**Required Competencies**

* Strong leadership and team-building skills.
* Strategic thinking and business acumen.
* Excellent problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
* Results-oriented with a continuous improvement mindset.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
* High level of accountability and integrity.

**Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**

* OSHA Recordable Incident Rate
* Lost Time Accident Rate
* On-Time Delivery Performance
* Production Throughput
* Scrap and Yield Performance
* Cost Per Ton Produced
* Machine Utilization
* Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE)
* Customer Quality Performance
* Employee Retention and Engagement
* Maintenance Downtime
* EBITDA/Operating Profit Contribution

**Physical and Work Environment Requirements**

* Frequent presence in foundry and machine shop environments.
* Exposure to heat, noise, dust, moving equipment, and industrial hazards.
* Ability to walk production areas daily and occasionally climb stairs, ladders, and platforms.
* Ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE).

We are seeking an experienced **NPI Director North America - Solutions** to provide regional leadership for New Product Introduction across North America, covering the relevant manufacturing sites and Design Center capabilities. The role translates business and customer priorities into a coherent NPI strategy, governance model and project portfolio, ensuring that new products move from concept to stable commercialization with the required quality, cost, timing, compliance and manufacturability. The role aligns Commercial, Global Design Center, NPI, Engineering, R&D, Quality, Procurement and Manufacturing and develops the capabilities required for consistent execution across sites..

**Key Responsibilities:**

**NPI strategy and governance**

* Translate the global NPI strategy into the North American operating model, stage-gate governance, priorities and decision routines, aligned with the Global Accounts and Global Design Center Director.
* Own the North American NPI portfolio and facilitate prioritization, resource allocation, escalation and trade-off decisions across customer programs and manufacturing sites in the region.
* Implement and continuously improve common global standards, templates, performance measures and management routines for product development, prototyping, design transfer, validation and industrialization.
* Ensure early NPI and Design Center involvement in strategic customer opportunities and new product concepts.

**Portfolio delivery and industrialization**

* Oversee major and complex NPI programs from concept through commercialization and stable production handover.
* Ensure projects have clear business cases, requirements, milestones, risks, accountabilities and readiness criteria.
* Drive design-for-manufacturing, cost engineering, value engineering and manufacturability reviews before production commitment.
* Ensure product concepts are technically feasible, compliant, financially viable and transferable across the relevant North American manufacturing network, while ensuring effective transfer to or from other regions when required.
* Lead executive-level reviews of portfolio status, critical risks, capacity constraints and recovery plans.

**Cross-functional and customer leadership**

* Act as the senior NPI interface for strategic customer programs and align customer expectations with operational capabilities.
* Build strong collaboration across Commercial, Business Development, Design, Engineering, R&D, Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain and Manufacturing.
* Coordinate North American and global resources to resolve cross-functional issues and accelerate decision making.
* Promote disciplined change control and transparent communication throughout the development and industrialization process.

**Capability and team leadership**

* Lead, coach and develop the North American NPI organization with teams in Seattle, Dallas and East-Longmeadow, including regional managers, project leaders and specialist resources.
* Build project management, product industrialization, risk management and technical problem-solving capabilities.
* Contribute to global communities of practice and promote best-practice sharing across North American sites and with other regions.
* Foster a culture of customer focus, innovation, accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.

**Qualifications and Requirements:**

* Master’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, product development, business or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* Significant leadership experience in NPI, product development, engineering, industrialization or complex program management within a multi-site manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated experience establishing governance, managing portfolios and leading major cross-functional product introductions.
* Strong commercial awareness and ability to balance customer value, technical feasibility, operational risk and financial performance.
* Excellent communication, influencing and decision-making skills in an international and multicultural environment.
* Fluent professional English; additional languages are an advantage. Ability to travel across North America and internationally when required.

existing_roles.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril's family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

**ABOUT THE JOB** 
 
As the Director of Manufacturing Engineering, your role encompasses the strategic oversight and tactical management of manufacturing engineering and systems to support both the development of new products and the scaling of high-volume production in Waltham, MA. You are charged with ensuring rigorous manufacturing processes are in place, resulting in the consistent delivery of superior quality products to our customers. Your leadership will also guarantee the fulfillment of manufacturing's capacity commitments while driving advancements in digital tools and methodologies to improve design, analysis, and execution. This role demands an innovative and adaptable approach to solving complex manufacturing challenges in a highly dynamic environment. 
 
**WHAT YOU'LL DO:**

* **Build & Lead the Manufacturing Engineering Team:** Recruit, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of manufacturing engineers and technical staff. Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across the organization.
* **Drive Manufacturing Strategy & Technology:** Develop and implement a long-term manufacturing engineering strategy aligned with Anduril Imaging's growth objectives. Drive adoption of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools to enhance efficiency and scalability across development and high-volume production.
* **Lead New Product Introduction (NPI):** Partner with R&D and product development teams to ensure seamless transition of new products from design to production. Champion Design for Manufacturability (DfM) and Design for Assembly (DfA) principles early in the development cycle to de-risk production scaling.
* **Scale Production Capability:** Evaluate, plan, and prioritize supply chain, production, and test optimizations to ensure the value stream can reliably meet production output goals. Develop business cases for vertical integration or supplier diversification where strategic partnerships will accelerate scalability.
* **Drive Continuous Improvement & Complexity Reduction:** Lead initiatives to improve yield, reduce cycle time, and lower cost across the manufacturing value chain. Drive commonality optimization, component and supplier rationalization, and process standardization to simplify production at scale.
* **Resource & Budget Management:** Manage budgets, staffing, and capital equipment planning for the manufacturing engineering organization. Forecast headcount and operational needs to support rapid scaling, including classified production environments.

#### **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field; Master's degree or MBA preferred.
* 12+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing engineering and operations, with at least 5 years in a leadership role managing manufacturing engineering teams.
* Demonstrated experience owning manufacturing value chains for complex electro-mechanical or imaging hardware — defense, aerospace, or adjacent industries strongly preferred.

**Job Summary**

**We are seeking a Director of Operations** **to join our River Valley team! The Director of Operations is responsible for leading a designated region of primary care clinics. This role oversees the performance, growth, and day-to-day operations of multiple clinic locations while ensuring exceptional patient care, financial performance, compliance, and operational excellence. existing_roles.title: Plant Manager III
existing_roles.description:
EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions helping industrial, infrastructure and defense customers address critical power and operational needs. The company delivers integrated solutions that combine energy storage technologies, power electronics, software-enabled intelligence, technical expertise and comprehensive global customer support. EnerSys supports customers across communications networks, data centers, energy infrastructure, material handling, transportation, aerospace and defense — including applications where power continuity is essential. Serving customers in more than 100 countries, EnerSys helps organizations manage energy more reliably, efficiently and intelligently in complex operating environments where uptime, safety and resilience matter.

 

**Job Purpose**
---------------

The Plant Manager will provide overall leadership for the phased development, start-up, ramp-up, and ongoing operation of the new lithium-ion cell manufacturing facility in Greenville, South Carolina. This is a unique opportunity to build a factory and its organization from the ground up in a fast-paced, highly dynamic environment.

The role will evolve through multiple phases of the project, beginning with facility construction and operational readiness and progressing through equipment installation and commissioning, production launch, workforce ramp-up, stabilization, and full-scale manufacturing operations.

The Plant Manager will be accountable for establishing the operating model, leadership capability, organizational structure, culture, management systems, and performance disciplines required to achieve excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, people, and customer satisfaction.

This leader must bring broad manufacturing expertise in a high-volume, fully automated environment and understand the interdependencies across production, engineering, maintenance, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, finance, and people. The successful candidate will combine strong operational and financial acumen with knowledge of lithium-ion cell manufacturing and a demonstrated ability to build organizations, develop leaders, anticipate workforce needs, and establish strong relationships with employees, customers, suppliers, and business partners.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------------

**Factory Development, Start-Up & Operational Readiness**

* Provide operational leadership throughout the phased development of the Greenville facility, ensuring manufacturing and operational requirements are incorporated as the factory is constructed, commissioned, launched, and scaled.
* Partner with Engineering, Project Management, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, EHS, People & Culture, IT/OT, and other functions to establish comprehensive manufacturing readiness.
* Translate facility and project milestones into executable operational plans covering equipment, processes, workforce, training, materials, systems, safety, quality, and infrastructure.
* Ensure equipment, manufacturing processes, systems, organizational capability, and workforce readiness progress together so that potential gaps are identified and resolved before they impact production.
* Establish the operating systems, standard work, governance, performance metrics, escalation processes, and accountability required to transition successfully from project execution into manufacturing operations.
* Lead the operational transition through equipment installation and commissioning, qualification, production launch, ramp-up, stabilization, and full-scale operations.

**Manufacturing & Operational Leadership**

* Provide end-to-end leadership of plant operations with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, capacity, employee performance, and overall manufacturing results.
* Maintain a comprehensive understanding of plant operating processes and ensure effective integration across production, maintenance, engineering, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, and supporting functions.
* Establish a culture of operational excellence, disciplined execution, accountability, continuous improvement, and structured problem solving.
* Establish and continuously evaluate plant KPIs to identify performance gaps, determine root causes, and drive sustainable corrective actions.
* Drive improvement in manufacturing productivity, equipment effectiveness, reliability, throughput, yield, quality, labor efficiency, and operating cost.
* Ensure appropriate manufacturing systems, controls, procedures, and escalation mechanisms are established as production volume and organizational complexity increase.
* Champion Lean manufacturing principles and create a culture in which continuous improvement is embedded throughout the organization.

**Lithium-Ion Cell Manufacturing**

* Provide leadership within a technically complex lithium-ion cell manufacturing environment.
* Apply practical knowledge of cell manufacturing processes, automated manufacturing equipment, process controls, materials, quality requirements, and production risks to operational decision-making.
* Work closely with Cell Engineering, Process Engineering, Quality, EHS, and other technical teams to establish safe, repeatable, high-quality manufacturing processes capable of operating at scale.
* Ensure plant teams understand the relationships among process capability, product quality, yield, throughput, equipment performance, manufacturing cost, and customer requirements.
* Support the effective introduction, industrialization, and scale-up of new manufacturing processes and technologies.

**Financial & Business Leadership**
-----------------------------------

* Own plant operating performance from both an operational and financial perspective.
* Develop and manage plant operating budgets, forecasts, labor plans, productivity targets, capital requirements, and cost-improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrate strong understanding of the economic drivers of manufacturing and translate operational performance into financial and business outcomes.
* Partner closely with Finance to understand and manage manufacturing cost, labor, productivity, inventory, scrap, yield, capital utilization, and other key plant performance drivers.
* Evaluate significant operational decisions through both manufacturing and financial lenses, balancing immediate execution requirements with the long-term capability and competitiveness of the plant.
* Establish strong cost-management and financial disciplines as the facility transitions from construction and start-up investment to sustainable manufacturing operations.

**Workforce Planning & Organizational Capability**

* Build the plant organization in phases aligned with facility construction, commissioning, production launch, ramp-up, and future operating requirements.
* Develop short- and long-term workforce plans to ensure the plant has the appropriate leadership, technical, skilled-trades, professional, and manufacturing capabilities required at each stage of growth.
* Anticipate talent, capacity, skill, and leadership gaps before they become constraints to manufacturing performance or future growth.
* Partner closely with People & Culture to develop recruiting, workforce planning, onboarding, training, retention, employee engagement, talent management, and organizational capability strategies.
* Establish clear organizational structures, decision rights, accountabilities, and leadership responsibilities as the facility grows and becomes operational.
* Develop workforce flexibility and organizational depth to mitigate single points of dependency and ensure business continuity.
* Regularly assess whether workforce capacity and capability are appropriately aligned with production requirements, operating plans, and future growth.

**Leadership Development & Succession**

* Recruit, build, coach, and develop a high-performing plant leadership team capable of successfully operating at increasing levels of scale and complexity.
* Establish a leadership culture where leaders are expected not only to deliver results but also to develop other leaders and build capability within their organizations.
* Partner with People & Culture to regularly assess leadership capability, organizational effectiveness, succession coverage, bench strength, and future talent requirements.
* Build strong succession pipelines for critical plant leadership and technical positions and ensure appropriate development plans are established for potential successors.
* Identify and develop high-potential talent through coaching, mentoring, expanded responsibilities, cross-functional experience, and targeted development opportunities.
* Establish sufficient leadership and technical depth to minimize organizational vulnerability and ensure continuity as the facility grows.
* Create a culture where talent development and succession planning are ongoing leadership responsibilities rather than periodic HR activities.

**Customer, Supplier & Stakeholder Leadership**
-----------------------------------------------

* Build strong, credible, long-term relationships with customers and ensure plant execution consistently supports quality, delivery, responsiveness, and customer commitments.
* Build strategic relationships with suppliers, equipment manufacturers, contractors, and other external partners critical to the construction, start-up, and ongoing operation of the plant.
* Work collaboratively with customers and suppliers to resolve issues quickly while protecting long-term business relationships.
* Serve as a senior representative of the Greenville operation with business leadership, customers, suppliers, community stakeholders, and other external partners as appropriate.
* Build strong cross-functional relationships across the broader organization and effectively navigate a complex, matrixed environment.
* Maintain a visible leadership presence throughout the plant and foster an employee environment built on communication, engagement, trust, accountability, and strong employee relations.

**Safety, Quality & Culture**

* Establish safety as a foundational operating principle and ensure appropriate systems, behaviors, and leadership accountability are embedded throughout the facility.
* Champion a quality-first mindset and ensure the organization consistently meets internal requirements and customer expectations.
* Build a high-performance culture characterized by accountability, collaboration, transparency, urgency, ownership, and continuous improvement.
* Establish clear expectations for leadership behavior and ensure those expectations cascade throughout the plant organization.
* Create an environment where employees understand how their work contributes to plant performance, customer success, and the broader business.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Business, or a related discipline.
* Significant progressive leadership experience within complex, high-volume, highly automated, or advanced manufacturing environments.
* Demonstrated experience leading a significant manufacturing operation with accountability across safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, people, and financial performance.
* Demonstrated experience supporting or leading the build and start-up of a new manufacturing facility, significant plant expansion, major manufacturing transformation, or complex production ramp-up.
* Strong knowledge of lithium-ion cell manufacturing or relevant advanced manufacturing technologies and processes.
* Broad understanding of manufacturing operations and the interdependencies among production, engineering, maintenance, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, finance, and people.
* Strong financial and commercial acumen with experience managing operating budgets, forecasts, manufacturing costs, capital investments, productivity, and business performance.
* Demonstrated success building, leading, coaching, and developing high-performing leadership teams.
* Experience with workforce planning, organizational design, talent development, and leadership succession.
* Demonstrated ability to build effective relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, executive leadership, and cross-functional partners.
* Proven ability to lead through ambiguity and rapidly changing priorities within a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
* Direct experience in lithium-ion cell manufacturing or large-scale battery manufacturing.
* Experience taking a newly constructed manufacturing facility through commissioning, production launch, volume ramp-up, and stabilized operations.
* Experience with highly automated manufacturing equipment and advanced manufacturing technologies.
* Strong working knowledge of Lean manufacturing, structured problem solving, operational excellence, and continuous-improvement methodologies.
* Experience working within a global manufacturing organization or complex matrixed business environment.

**General Job Requirements**
----------------------------

* This position requires working in a plant/warehouse environment. Therefore, expect varying working conditions.

existing_roles.title: Senior Manager, Fulfillment and Logistics Operations, Ford Energy
existing_roles.description:
**Overview**
------------

At Ford, you’ll work on ideas that matter, alongside passionate people who want to make a global impact. Together, we’re shaping the next era of transportation—grounded in purpose, driven by progress. Make your move.

* Job Type: Full time
* Work Type: Hybrid

 

We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters.

 

Ford Energy is a newly formed, wholly-owned subsidiary of Ford Motor Company dedicated to accelerating U.S. energy independence. Leveraging Ford’s century of manufacturing excellence and world-class battery energy storage systems (BESS) technology, Ford Energy designs, manufactures, and services grid-scale and commercial DC battery energy storage systems (BESS). Ford Energy is uniquely positioned to capture the growing demand for reliable, US-built energy storage systems. We are not just building batteries; we are building the infrastructure for the next generation of the American grid.

Why Ford Energy?

At Ford Energy, you have the backing of an industrial manufacturing powerhouse with the agility of a dedicated energy startup offering industry leading technology. We offer a competitive compensation package including performance-based bonuses, Ford vehicle discounts, and the opportunity to shape the energy strategy of one of the world's most iconic brands.

**In this position...**

The Senior Manager, Fulfillment & Logistics Operations is a senior leadership role accountable for the end-to-end fulfillment, logistics, and parts supply performance of the Project Operations & Performance value stream. This leader sets the direction for inventory and supply planning, parts replenishment, warehousing, distribution, and outbound product shipping, and owns the service, cost, and working capital outcomes of the network. The role also delivers the digital capabilities that give customers real-time visibility into parts inventory, order status, and shipment information, making fulfillment a differentiator in the customer experience. Partnering with Product Creation & Industrialization, Finance, Sales, and Procurement, this leader combines deep supply chain and logistics expertise with change leadership and the ability to build high-performing teams, delivering measurable business impact. [Scope: add annual logistics and inventory spend, number of facilities and 3PL partners, and team size.]

**What you'll do...**

**1. Strategy & Transformation**
 

* Own the fulfillment and logistics strategy across the Project Operations & Performance value stream, aligned with growth and customer experience goals.
* Lead transformation from concept to measurable results, including integration with Product Creation & Industrialization.
* Champion the Voice of Customer, resolve issues quickly, and incorporate insights into product, service, and fulfillment improvements.

**2. Parts Supply, Inventory & Warehousing**
 

* Lead end-to-end spare parts planning, inventory, and distribution, balancing availability, cost-to-serve, and working capital.
* Optimize inventory through segment-specific safety stock and reorder strategies, procurement controls, and clearance of slow-moving stock.
* Hold warehouse partners accountable for inventory accuracy, productivity, and safety.
* Partner with Finance to improve inventory velocity and the cash conversion cycle.

**3. Outbound Logistics & Delivery**
 

* Own delivery performance from factory release to customer or site, establishing service targets and driving perfect-order execution.
* Manage carrier, freight forwarder, and 3PL relationships, including contracts, rates, capacity, mode selection, and performance reviews.
* Ensure battery energy storage shipments meet hazardous materials and oversize/overweight transport requirements, including DOT, packaging, labeling, documentation, and permits.
* Coordinate production, shipping, installation, and site readiness across Sales, Manufacturing, Customer Project Teams, and Finance; resolve delays, damage claims, and exceptions.
* Reduce freight costs and lead times through route optimization, load consolidation, and standardized, system-integrated workflows.

**4. Digital Capabilities & Customer Visibility**
 

* Deliver customer self-service access to parts availability, consumption, order status, shipment tracking, and estimated delivery.
* Partner with IT, Product, and Sales to connect ERP, planning, warehouse, and carrier data through customer portals and API/EDI integrations.
* Provide proactive alerts for delays, backorders, and delivery changes; measure adoption, satisfaction, and reductions in order-status inquiries.
* Replace manual processes with automated workflows using SAP, advanced planning systems, and integrated data.

**5. Supplier & Production Alignment**
 

* Partner with Procurement to monitor Tier 1 and Tier 2 supplier performance and mitigate material risks before they disrupt production.
* Align factory priorities with high-value customer orders and strategic inventory needs.

**6. Leadership, Performance & Continuous Improvement**
 

* Build and develop a high-performing fulfillment, logistics, and supply chain team.
* Present performance, risks, and investment cases to senior leadership and align cross-functional stakeholders.
* Own KPIs such as OTIF, forecast accuracy, inventory turns, backorders, fill rate, lead time, and cost-to-serve; quantify the financial and operational impact of improvements.
* Improve service and field performance through shorter repair cycles, higher first-time-fix rates, and greater product reliability.
* Lead change adoption and apply Lean and Six Sigma methods to eliminate waste and reduce fulfillment lead times.

**You'll have...**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations, Business Administration, or at least 10 years' of experience in a related field
* 8+ years of progressive experience in aftermarket operations, service supply chain, fulfillment, or logistics, including leading managers and multi-functional teams.
* Proven record of leading large-scale operational or digital transformation initiatives across multi-functional teams.
* Deep expertise in spare parts planning, inventory management, warehousing, distribution, and outbound logistics.
* Financial acumen, including budget ownership and working capital management.
* Executive-level communication and influencing skills, with the ability to partner with and present to stakeholders at all levels.
* Must be able to travel 50% as needed

**Even better, you'll have...**

* Master's Degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or APICS CPIM certification is a plus.
* Experience in the automotive or heavy equipment aftermarket/service industry.
* Experience delivering customer-facing digital capabilities, such as portals, order and shipment visibility tools, or API/EDI integrations.
* Experience in transportation, outbound logistics, or freight management, including hazardous materials or oversize/overweight shipping.
* Knowledge of project management methodologies (e.g., Agile).
* Experience working with Salesforce and/or SAP S4 HANA.
* Experience in high-mix, global manufacturing or consumer/industrial industries.

**Additional Information:**

Work Location: Dearborn or Kentucky (United States), but the company is willing to consider a hybrid modality

Required Travel: Up to 50% travel required

You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you think you can bring value to Ford Motor Company, we encourage you to apply!

As an established global company, we offer the benefit of choice. You can choose what your Ford future will look like: will your story span the globe, or keep you close to home? Will your career be a deep dive into what you love, or a series of new teams and new skills? Will you be a leader, a changemaker, a technical expert, a culture builder…or all of the above? No matter what you choose, we offer a work life that works for you, including:
 

* Immediate medical, dental, vision and prescription drug coverage
* Flexible family care days, paid parental leave, new parent ramp-up programs, subsidized back-up child care and more
* Family building benefits including adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, fertility treatments, and more
* Vehicle discount program for employees and family members and management leases
* Tuition assistance
* Established and active employee resource groups
* Paid time off for individual and team community service
* A generous schedule of paid holidays, including the week between Christmas and New Year’s Day
* Paid time off and the option to purchase additional vacation time.

This position is leadership level 5 and ranges from $141,700-$268,300.

Final determination of salary grade will be based on candidate's skills and experience, and base salary will be set within the applicable range according to job scope, responsibility and competitive market value.

For more information on salary and benefits, click here: https://fordcareers.co/LL5

For more information on salary and benefits, click here: https://fordcareers.co/GSR

Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Candidates for positions with Ford Motor Company must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, age, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability status or protected veteran status. In the United States, if you need a reasonable accommodation for the online application process due to a disability, please call 1-888-336-0660.

protected_roles.title: Quality Management Director
protected_roles.description:
**Overview**

The Quality Management Director develops, implements, and maintains the hospital's Quality Management System in line with ISO 9001 and NIAHO standards. The director oversees the Quality Assurance/Performance Improvement (QAPI) program and keeps the hospital compliant with CMS Conditions of Participation and state requirements. The role leads survey and accreditation readiness, including mock surveys, tracers, and plans of correction. The director chairs or coordinates the quality committees, supervises the Quality and Compliance Associate, and monitors regulatory quality requirements. The director also oversees quality and patient safety data reporting, including dashboards and benchmarking, presented to the Medical Staff, Executive Leadership, and Board.

I. Minimum Qualifications:

A. Education:

1. Current licensure to practice as a Registered Professional Nurse in the State of Texas or equivalent degree in healthcare with a minimum of a baccalaureate degree. Master's degree in nursing, healthcare administration, quality management, or a related healthcare field preferred.

2. Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or higher) preferred.

3. Must have at least three (3) years of experience in management or quality improvement in an accredited acute care setting.

II. Knowledge and Skills:

1. Demonstrate knowledge and leadership skills to perform duties outlined in the job description

1. Must have strong knowledge of accrediting and regulatory agency requirements

2. Must have good problem solving, interpersonal communication and project management skills

3. Must be extremely detail-oriented with respect to documentation and communication

4. Able to read and interpret medical record documentation and hospital policies and procedures

5. Must have at a minimum proficient computer skills in using Microsoft computer programs (Word, Excel, PPT, etc.)

III. Personal/Physical Requirements:

1. Mental and physical health to meet demands of position

2. Must have respect for human dignity and cultural diversity

3. Demonstrates ability in use of verbal/written communication, and effectively communicate with patients, families, hospital staff, medical staff, and general public.

IV. Data Reporting Requirements:

1. Oversees and supports the data collection, validation, analysis, and submits required quality and patient safety data to regulatory, accrediting, and governmental agencies (e.g., CMS, Texas Health and Human Services, and the hospital's accrediting organization) within required timeframes, including all mandatory quality reporting program measures applicable to a rural hospital.

Weaver Popcorn is seeking a seasoned quality leader ready to step into a broader Director-level role. The Director of Quality provides strategic and operational leadership for food safety, quality assurance, regulatory compliance, audit readiness, and continuous improvement across the organization’s food manufacturing operations. This leader will strengthen and standardize quality systems, develop quality talent, and partner with plant and business leaders to ensure products consistently meet company, customer, certification, and regulatory requirements.

This is a hands-on leadership role for an experienced food manufacturing quality professional who can set direction while remaining actively engaged with plant teams, audits, investigations, corrective actions, and day-to-day execution.

**HOW WILL YOU HELP US GROW?**
==============================

**Quality & Food Safety Leadership**
------------------------------------

* Develop and lead the company’s quality and food safety strategy, priorities, policies, procedures, and performance expectations across manufacturing locations.
* Ensure quality assurance and food safety programs are effectively implemented, maintained, verified, and continuously improved.
* Establish and oversee grain and popcorn quality standards from grower receipt and bulk storage through processing, bagging, and shipment, ensuring consistent quality controls throughout the supply chain.
* Provide visible leadership on the manufacturing floor through routine plant engagement, risk reviews, verification activities, and follow-up on quality concerns.
* Build a culture of accountability, prevention, compliance, and continuous improvement across Quality, Operations, Supply Chain, Sales, and other partner functions.

**SQF, Audits & Regulatory Compliance**
---------------------------------------

* Lead and maintain SQF certification programs, including system ownership, audit preparation, certification readiness, corrective actions, and ongoing compliance.
* Plan, lead, and oversee internal, customer, certification, and regulatory audits of food manufacturing facilities.
* Ensure timely closure of audit findings, nonconformances, corrective and preventive actions, and related verification activities.
* Lead cross-functional Food Safety/HACCP, risk assessment, prerequisite program, and food quality teams.
* Monitor applicable food safety and quality requirements and translate them into practical operating standards and controls.
* Ensure effective quality controls for bulk grain storage, bin holds and releases, sampling, testing, and corn disposition prior to processing, including compliance with applicable phytosanitary requirements.

**Quality Management Systems**
------------------------------

* Own the effective use and continuous improvement of quality management system software, including document control, audits, corrective actions, training records, verification, and reporting.
* Standardize quality documentation, specifications, procedures, policies, records, and reporting across facilities.
* Use quality data, trend analysis, and leading and lagging indicators to identify risk, establish priorities, and improve performance.
* Ensure effective controls for ingredient sampling, product verification, environmental monitoring, sanitation verification, traceability, and other core quality programs.
* Provide oversight of corn testing and laboratory quality programs, including mycotoxin testing, internal and third-party sample testing, review of test results, and appropriate product disposition based on quality and food safety requirements.

**People Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership**
----------------------------------------------------

* Lead, coach, and develop a quality team of at least two direct reports, with potential for broader team responsibility as the function grows.
* Set clear goals, define accountabilities, assess performance, strengthen technical capability, and create development plans for quality team members.
* Partner with Plant Managers and Operations leaders to resolve quality issues without compromising food safety, customer requirements, or regulatory compliance.
* Establish and enforce hold/release and product disposition standards, with authority to stop processing or bagging operations and place grain, ingredients, or finished product on hold when food safety or quality requirements are not met.
* Partner with Sales and Customer Service to respond to customer documentation requests, audits, samples, complaints, and quality-related inquiries.
* Lead investigations into customer complaints, product or process deviations, and recurring issues; ensure root cause analysis and sustainable corrective action.
* Oversee nonconforming material, product holds, rework, release, and disposition processes, partnering with Operations and suppliers to ensure timely resolution and prevent recurrence.
* Provide clear quality updates, risk assessments, recommendations, and performance reporting to senior leadership and other decision-makers.

**WHAT DO YOU NEED TO HAVE?**
=============================

* Bachelor's degree in food science, Food Safety, Microbiology, Chemistry, Biology, Engineering, or related fields.
* 8–10+ years of progressive quality or food safety experience in the food manufacturing industry.
* At least 5 years of people-management experience, including progressive supervisory and manager-level responsibility.
* Proven leadership of SQF certification programs and successful food manufacturing audits.
* Demonstrated knowledge of food safety principles, quality assurance procedures and policies, HACCP-based programs, risk assessment, corrective action, and preventive controls.
* Experience leading internal, customer, certification, and/or regulatory audits across food manufacturing environments.
* Hands-on experience with quality management system software and electronic quality records.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through influence, develop teams, manage competing priorities, and drive consistent execution across locations.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate quality risk and technical requirements to operational and executive audiences.
* Ability to travel regularly to manufacturing facilities and business locations, as needed.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Experience in grain, corn, popcorn, milling, ingredient, or related agricultural processing.
* SQF Practitioner experience and formal training in HACCP, PCQI, internal auditing, root cause analysis, or preventive controls.
* Experience supporting multiple manufacturing sites or standardizing quality systems across locations.
* Experience with supplier quality, customer complaint management, environmental monitoring, traceability, recall readiness, and food defense programs.

**WHAT DOES SUCCESS LOOK LIKE?**
================================

* Consistent audit and certification readiness across facilities.
* Stronger standardization and adoption of quality systems, procedures, and records.
* Timely, well-documented corrective action with verified effectiveness.
* Reduced recurrence of quality issues and customer complaints through disciplined root cause analysis.
* A capable, accountable quality team with clear goals and development plans.
* Credible, practical partnership with Operations and business leaders while maintaining independent quality judgment.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT & SCHEDULE**
===============================

This role operates across office and food manufacturing environments and requires regular presence in production areas. The typical schedule is Monday through Friday; however, the Director of Quality must be available outside normal business hours, including occasional evenings or weekends, when operational, audit, customer, or food safety needs require support. Regular travel is expected based on business needs.

**HOW WILL WE HELP YOU GROW?**
==============================

* Competitive compensation.
* Three weeks of paid time off in the first year.
* 401(k) plan with a company match of 100% of employee deferrals up to 10%.
* Health, vision, dental, life, and disability insurance beginning the first day of the month following 30 days of employment.
* Education reimbursement of up to $15,000 per year.

**EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY**
================================

Weaver Popcorn is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and associates. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without regard to any status protected by applicable law.

*The role responsibilities are many, various, and not limited to those written in this document*

At **Valley Oaks Health**, quality improvement is about more than meeting standards—it’s about using data, collaboration, and continuous learning to make care better for the people and communities we serve.

We’re looking for a **Quality Improvement Director** to lead our organization-wide Quality Improvement and Quality Assurance (QI/QA) efforts and help turn information into meaningful, measurable improvements in care, outcomes, and operations.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead Valley Oaks Health’s QI/QA program, annual quality improvement plan, and organization-wide improvement initiatives.
* Use clinical outcomes, performance data, patient experience, safety events, quality reviews, and operational trends to identify opportunities for improvement.
* Develop and monitor meaningful quality measures, dashboards, scorecards, and other tools that help leaders understand performance and take action.
* Lead quality efforts supporting our **FQHC Look-Alike and integrated care programs**, including required measures, assessments, reporting, and continuous improvement activities.
* Partner with clinical, operational, MIS, Compliance, HIM, Community Health, and executive leaders to strengthen quality and performance across the organization.
* Lead and develop QI staff while building a culture where continuous improvement and quality are shared responsibilities.

**What You'll Bring:**

* Master’s degree in Public Health, Health Administration, Nursing, Social Work, or a related field preferred; bachelor’s degree with significant QI and healthcare compliance experience required.
* **5+ years of experience** in quality improvement, healthcare compliance, or a related role.
* FQHC or integrated healthcare experience highly preferred, particularly within behavioral health and/or primary care.
* Knowledge of quality improvement methodologies such as Lean or Six Sigma and healthcare quality measures.
* Strong data analysis and reporting skills, including the ability to turn data into actionable insights; experience with Excel and Power BI preferred.
* Knowledge of HRSA, FQHC Look-Alike, healthcare regulatory, and quality requirements.
* Strong leadership, communication, collaboration, organization, and problem-solving skills.

**Why Valley Oaks Health?**

At Valley Oaks Health, our work is grounded in our core values:

**Be Brave. Be Human. Be Connected.**

We’re looking for a leader who brings those values to quality improvement—someone who is willing to ask difficult questions, brings people together to solve problems, and uses data not just to measure performance, but to make meaningful change.

If you’re a collaborative quality leader who is passionate about **turning data into action, strengthening systems, and continually improving the care we provide, we’d love to hear from you!**

protected_roles.title: Head of Quality
protected_roles.description:
**About Tutor**

We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But, nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robot Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Our robot Sonny does handwork, using two arms to achieve human-like dexterity in picking and packing. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable, and faster to put to work.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

**Why Tutor?**

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

**The Role**

Tutor is hiring a Head of Quality to lead quality as a function, alongside the Head of Manufacturing. You own the quality system, supplier quality across our supply base, product safety certifications, and the quality targets the company holds itself to. The quality engineers and the quality manager report to you, and you grow the team from there. You report to the CTO. As our operations organization grows, you and the Head of Manufacturing will report to the leader of that organization.

This is a building role. The first pieces, incoming inspection, supplier controls and failure analysis, are being put in place by the team you will lead. Your job is to turn them into a system that holds as production grows, a supplier base we can trust, and a quality record that customers and certifying bodies can verify. You have the authority to hold any shipment that is not right.

### **Requirements**

* You have led a quality function at a company that builds complex electromechanical hardware in volume
* You have built or rebuilt a quality system and taken it through ISO 9001 or an equivalent certification
* You have run supplier quality across a supply base, including suppliers overseas
* You have taken a product through product safety certification
* You have built and led a team of quality engineers and managers
* You make decisions from data, and you can hold a shipment when the data says so

### **Nice to haves**

* Robotics, automation, vehicles, or capital equipment
* Reliability engineering methods: life testing, failure rate analysis, design reviews
* Building quality data and tooling that other teams use
* Experience with manufacturing execution systems

### **Benefits**

* **Fully employer-covered health insurance**, so you’re protected without the premium.
* **A managed 401(k)** to help you plan for the future.
* **Generous time off:** unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
* **Regular in-office meals** and team social events throughout the year.

**Compensation**

The base salary range for this role is $220,000 to $280,000, depending on experience.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

*Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.*
